domain: Flight operations for the crewed deep-space vessel Aurelian on a Mars transit; current anomaly at T+248 days is a pressure drop on ECLSS Coolant Loop B risking a cabin thermal rise.

documents.title: Anomaly Report ANOM-HAL-003: Bus A Distribution Fault and Loss of Pump P-203 (Halley)
documents.summary: A failed power MOSFET dropped Bus A on the Halley flight, taking Coolant Pump P-203 with it. The fault was isolated, Bus A cross-tied to Bus B with load shed, and P-203 repowered, preventing a coolant-loop loss.

documents.title: Anomaly Report ANOM-HAL-011: Coolant Loop B Slow Pressure Decay — Accumulator Bladder Permeation (Halley)
documents.summary: On the Halley flight, Coolant Loop B pressure decayed slowly from 310 to 261 kPa over eleven hours. Root cause was GN2 permeation and partial bladder failure in accumulator ACC-2. The loop was isolated and the mission completed on single-loop cooling.

documents.title: Anomaly Report ANOM-HAL-018: Slow MMH Leak at an RCS Valve Fitting (Halley)
documents.summary: A slow MMH leak at an RCS valve fitting on the Halley flight was isolated to the RCS branch by closing PV-1, protecting the main propellant tanks and preserving the Mars Orbit Insertion capability.

documents.title: Anomaly Report ANOM-KEP-009: Star Tracker ST-1 Stuck Bright-Object Flag and Attitude Excursion (Kepler)
documents.summary: A stuck bright-object flag on star tracker ST-1 dropped it from the attitude solution on the Kepler flight, causing a brief attitude excursion and secondary loss of the high-gain link. Recovered on single-tracker operation and by clearing the flag.

documents.title: Anomaly Report ANOM-KEP-014: Coolant Loop A Pump Cavitation from Gas Ingress (Kepler)
documents.summary: On the Kepler flight, Pump P-203 on Coolant Loop A developed cavitation from GN2 entrained after an accumulator recharge. Root cause was a high-point gas pocket not bled before restart. Resolved by gas bleed at the high-point vent.

documents.title: Anomaly Report ANOM-KEP-022: Radiator Panel 3 Micrometeoroid Puncture and Loop B Coolant Leak (Kepler)
documents.summary: A micrometeoroid punctured Radiator Panel 3 on the Kepler flight, producing a monotonic coolant leak on Loop B with falling accumulator quantity. The punctured panel was isolated, preserving the second Loop B panel and returning the loop to reduced service.

documents.title: Anomaly Report ANOM-PTO-007: Cabin Thermal Rise from CHX-1 Fouling (Ptolemy)
documents.summary: On the Ptolemy flight, cabin temperature climbed to 28.9 C with coolant loop pressures nominal. Root cause was progressive fouling of the cabin heat exchanger CHX-1 restricting coolant flow. Resolved by flow balancing, not loop isolation.

documents.title: Anomaly Report ANOM-PTO-031: Solar Conjunction Blackout During a Trajectory Correction Burn (Ptolemy)
documents.summary: A trajectory correction burn on the Ptolemy flight was executed through a solar-conjunction communications blackout on a pre-loaded sequence. The burn completed nominally with no ground link, validating the burn-blackout flight rule.

documents.title: Flight Director Log — Gold Shift, T+230: TCM-4 Trajectory Correction Burn
documents.summary: Gold-shift narrative of the TCM-4 mid-course correction, a routine burn executed through a planned high-gain dropout on a pre-loaded sequence, exercising FR-COMM-2.3 ahead of the Mars Orbit Insertion.

documents.title: Flight Director Log — Silver Shift, T+243: Routine Cruise and ECLSS Baseline
documents.summary: Silver-shift routine cruise narrative five days before the Loop B anomaly, documenting the nominal ECLSS baseline including a steady Loop B accumulator precharge, a nominal momentum dump, and a clean DSRN station handover.

documents.title: Flight Director Log — Gold Shift, T+248: Coolant Loop B Pressure Drop and Isolation
documents.summary: Gold-shift flight director narrative of the T+248 Coolant Loop B pressure drop: the leak-versus-gas diagnosis, the failed accumulator recharges, the isolation at the sustained-decay criterion, and the transition to a stable single-loop condition.

documents.title: Flight Director Log — Silver Shift, T+249: Single-Loop Operations and Mars Approach Planning
documents.summary: Silver-shift narrative confirming the single-loop cabin thermal condition is stable, consumables are unaffected, and a first-look assessment shows the Mars Orbit Insertion burn remains within single-loop thermal capability.

documents.title: Flight Rule FR-ABORT-1.0: Abort and Return Criteria
documents.summary: Flight rules defining the conditions under which the mission aborts to a free-return or powered-return trajectory, based on loss of redundancy in survival systems, propellant shortfall against Mars Orbit Insertion, or consumables margin.

documents.title: Flight Rule FR-COMM-2.3: Communications Blackout During a Main Engine Burn
documents.summary: Flight rules for a loss of the communications link during a main-engine burn, establishing that a burn with a valid guidance solution is not aborted for loss of signal because the burn sequence executes autonomously onboard.

documents.title: Flight Rule FR-CONS-3.2: Consumables Margins
documents.summary: Flight rules defining required consumables margins for oxygen, water, food, and propellant, identifying water as the binding consumable at 74 days at T+248, and the accounting that feeds the abort criteria.

documents.title: Flight Rule FR-ECLSS-4.1: Coolant Loop Go / No-Go
documents.summary: Flight rules governing coolant-loop operation and isolation, including the pressure and decay-rate thresholds for loop isolation and the requirement to preserve one healthy loop at all times.

documents.title: Flight Rule FR-PWR-6.1: Power Margin Rules
documents.summary: Flight rules for electrical power margins, defining the single-source load limit during cross-tie, the essential loads that are never shed, and the battery reserve that must be protected.

documents.title: Flight Rule FR-THRM-5.4: Cabin Thermal Limits
documents.summary: Flight rules for cabin temperature, defining the 27 C caution, 30 C avionics limit, and 35 C survivability bound, and the actions required at each threshold during degraded cooling.

documents.title: Hazard Analysis HAZ-ECLSS-01: Loss of Both Coolant Loops and Cabin Thermal Runaway
documents.summary: Hazard analysis of the loss of both coolant loops leading to cabin thermal runaway, tracing the credible common-cause paths (power, gas ingress, MMOD) and the controls — loop and bus independence, isolation criteria, and the abort criterion of last resort.

documents.title: Hazard Analysis HAZ-MMOD-02: Micrometeoroid and Orbital Debris Strike
documents.summary: Hazard analysis of a micrometeoroid or debris strike, spanning radiator coolant leaks, cabin depressurization, and damage to arrays, antenna, or propellant tanks, with the controls of shielding, redundancy, and panel- and module-level isolation.

documents.title: Hazard Analysis HAZ-PROP-03: Hypergolic Propellant Leak and Crew Toxic Exposure
documents.summary: Hazard analysis of a monomethylhydrazine or nitrogen tetroxide leak, covering the toxic-exposure and mission-loss consequence paths and the controls of branch isolation, crew protection, and the propellant reserve protecting Mars Orbit Insertion.

documents.title: Malfunction Procedure MAL-COMM-02: Loss of Signal / Comms Blackout
documents.summary: Procedure for loss of signal, distinguishing attitude loss, solar conjunction, station gap, and onboard fault, and the actions to reacquire including the fallback to low-gain omnidirectional links.

documents.title: Malfunction Procedure MAL-ECLSS-03: Cabin Thermal Excursion
documents.summary: Procedure for a rising cabin temperature, covering load shed, single-loop cooling management, avionics protection at the 30 C limit, and the timeline that follows a coolant-loop isolation.

documents.title: Malfunction Procedure MAL-ECLSS-07: Coolant Loop Pressure Drop
documents.summary: Emergency procedure for a falling pressure in either coolant loop, covering leak-versus-gas-ingress diagnosis, accumulator recharge, and the go/no-go criteria for isolating the loop and transferring heat to the surviving loop.

documents.title: Malfunction Procedure MAL-ECLSS-09: Coolant Pump Fault
documents.summary: Procedure for a coolant pump fault — loss of flow, cavitation, or overspeed — including the distinction between a pump-mechanical fault and a power-side loss, and the transition to single-loop cooling.

documents.title: Malfunction Procedure MAL-ECLSS-11: Cabin Depressurization
documents.summary: Emergency procedure for a cabin pressure loss, covering leak-rate classification, module isolation, emergency repressurization, and the pressure thresholds at which the crew dons suits or retreats to the safe haven.

documents.title: Malfunction Procedure MAL-EPS-04: Power Bus Fault
documents.summary: Procedure for the loss or fault of a main power bus, covering fault isolation, the cross-tie decision, load shed to stay within single-source rating, and protection of the coolant pump on the affected bus.

documents.title: Malfunction Procedure MAL-GNC-05: Attitude Control / GNC Fault
documents.summary: Procedure for a GNC fault — star tracker disagreement, reaction wheel saturation, or loss of attitude reference — including the fallback to single-tracker and IMU propagation and the entry to Sun-pointing safe mode.

documents.title: Malfunction Procedure MAL-LIFE-01: Life Support Consumables Contingency
documents.summary: Procedure for a consumables shortfall — a water processor fault, scrubber degradation, or an oxygen/nitrogen loss — including the conservation actions and the tie to the consumables and abort flight rules.

documents.title: Malfunction Procedure MAL-PROP-06: Propellant Leak
documents.summary: Procedure for a suspected MMH or NTO propellant leak, covering detection, isolation of the affected propellant branch, crew protection from toxic hypergolic vapour, and assessment of the impact on the Mars Orbit Insertion burn.

documents.title: Malfunction Procedure MAL-THRM-08: Radiator Loss / Heat Rejection Fault
documents.summary: Procedure for degraded heat rejection from a radiator panel — micrometeoroid puncture, attitude view loss, or flow blockage — including panel isolation and the resulting reduction in cooling capacity.

documents.title: Nominal Procedure NOM-COMM-05: DSRN Station Handover
documents.summary: Routine procedure for handing the communications link between the three DSRN ground stations every eight hours, including the planned overlap, onboard recording during any gap, and playback on acquisition of signal.

documents.title: Nominal Procedure NOM-ECLSS-12: Coolant Loop Servicing and Accumulator Recharge
documents.summary: Routine procedure for servicing a coolant loop: verifying and restoring the accumulator GN2 precharge to 340 kPa, bleeding entrained gas at the high-point vent, and making up coolant to restore the 310 kPa nominal loop pressure.

documents.title: Nominal Procedure NOM-ECLSS-15: Coolant Loop Flow Balancing
documents.summary: Routine procedure for rebalancing coolant flow between cold plates and the cabin heat exchanger to correct uneven cooling or a mild flow restriction, as used to recover from the CHX-1 fouling event on the Ptolemy flight.

documents.title: Nominal Procedure NOM-EPS-02: Bus Load Management and Load Shed
documents.summary: Routine procedure for daily power configuration and the load-shed category list, defining which loads are shed and in what order to free up to 1.4 kW for cross-tie operation or single-loop cooling.

documents.title: Nominal Procedure NOM-GNC-04: Attitude Reference Update and Star Tracker Calibration
documents.summary: Routine procedure for updating the attitude reference, calibrating the star trackers against the IMU, and dumping reaction-wheel momentum, keeping HGA pointing within the 0.2 degree lock requirement.

documents.title: Nominal Procedure NOM-PROP-03: Main Engine Burn Preparation
documents.summary: Routine preparation for a main-engine burn — trajectory correction or Mars Orbit Insertion — including propellant and pressurization checks, burn-sequence load, attitude setup, and the communications and thermal effects of the burn attitude.

documents.title: Subsystem Specification: Avionics and Flight Computer Architecture
documents.summary: Specification for the Aurelian triple-redundant flight computer architecture, the caution and warning system, and the cold-plate cooling dependency that ties avionics health to the coolant loops and cabin thermal limits.

documents.title: Subsystem Specification: Communications and the Deep Space Relay Network Link
documents.summary: Specification for the Aurelian X-band and Ka-band communications system and its link to the three-station Deep Space Relay Network, including the T+248 one-way light time of 13.5 minutes and the causes and handling of loss of signal.

documents.title: Subsystem Specification: ECLSS Active Thermal Coolant Loops A and B
documents.summary: Design and operating specification for the Aurelian dual redundant single-phase coolant loops, including nominal pressures, alarm thresholds, pump and accumulator data, and the isolation criteria that govern loop safing.

documents.title: Subsystem Specification: Electrical Power System — Buses A and B
documents.summary: Specification for the Aurelian 120 VDC dual-bus electrical power system, including solar array and battery capacity, bus load limits, the cross-tie contactor, and the power dependency of the two coolant pumps.

documents.title: Subsystem Specification: Guidance, Navigation and Control
documents.summary: Specification for the Aurelian guidance, navigation and control system, including star trackers, the inertial measurement unit, four reaction wheels, and the attitude-hold requirements that couple GNC to thermal and communications performance.

documents.title: Subsystem Specification: Life Support and Consumables
documents.summary: Specification for the Aurelian atmosphere, water and consumables systems, including the regenerable CO2 scrubbers, oxygen and nitrogen partial-pressure setpoints, and the consumables margins that anchor the abort and go/no-go flight rules.

documents.title: Subsystem Specification: Main Propulsion and Reaction Control
documents.summary: Specification for the Aurelian bipropellant main engine and reaction control system, including thrust, Isp, propellant load, the Mars Orbit Insertion burn requirement, and propellant isolation for leak response.

documents.title: Subsystem Specification: Cabin Thermal Control and Heat Rejection
documents.summary: Specification for the Aurelian cabin thermal environment, radiator heat-rejection budget, and the single-loop degraded-cooling response, including cabin temperature limits and the projected thermal rise rate when Coolant Loop B is isolated.

documents.title: Voice Loop VOICE-248-01: Coolant Loop B Low-Pressure Caution Onset
documents.summary: CAPCOM-crew voice loop capturing the onset of the Coolant Loop B pressure drop at T+248, from the 285 kPa Low caution through the first trend readings and the leak-versus-gas-ingress diagnosis, with the 27-minute round-trip delay evident.

documents.title: Voice Loop VOICE-248-02: Coolant Loop B Isolation and Transition to Single-Loop Cooling
documents.summary: The isolation decision voice loop: after two accumulator recharges fail to hold, the crew hits the sustained decay criterion, closes MV-207, commands P-204 off, transfers heat to Loop A, and begins load shed under MAL-ECLSS-07 and MAL-ECLSS-03.

documents.title: Voice Loop VOICE-243-03: Nominal DSRN Station Handover and Shift Change
documents.summary: A routine voice loop capturing a nominal DSRN station handover from Cygnus to Draco with planned overlap, plus the crew shift-change status report five days before the coolant anomaly, establishing the pre-anomaly baseline.

documents.title: Voice Loop VOICE-230-04: Trajectory Correction Burn Go/No-Go Poll
documents.summary: The go/no-go poll for a mid-course trajectory correction burn, covering the pre-loaded burn sequence, propellant margin, and the crew's confirmation that a loss of signal will not abort a valid burn per FR-COMM-2.3.

documents.title: Voice Loop VOICE-249-05: Post-Isolation Consumables and Thermal Status
documents.summary: The day-after status loop following the Loop B isolation, confirming the single-loop cabin thermal condition is holding, consumables margins are unaffected, and the mission remains well clear of any abort criterion.
